elements.element: Audit frequency is limited to no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 expressly limits audits to “no more than once in any 12-month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days' notice before an audit.
Audit notice must be in writing.
Audits must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 expressly limits audits to “during business hours.”
Section 22.1 requires the audit to be conducted “by an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires the independent auditor to be “bound by confidentiality.”

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that “Vendor bears audit costs” as the default allocation.

elements.element: Audit costs may shift to Customer only if underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs to Customer only where the audit establishes underpayment “exceeding five percent for the audited period.”

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor may not directly access Customer systems.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 expressly provides that “Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly.”

elements.element: Audit frequency is limited to no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The stricter limit of no more than once in any rolling 12-month period satisfies the once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days' notice before an audit.
elements.evidence: The required 30 days' written notice exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that “Vendor bears audit costs” as the default allocation.

elements.element: Audit costs may shift to Customer only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts costs when underpayment exceeds 5%, rather than limiting cost shifting to underpayments exceeding 10%.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements every preferred requirement, including the rolling 12-month cap, 30 days' written notice, business-hours restriction, independent confidential auditor, 5% cost-shifting threshold, and prohibition on direct systems access. It does not satisfy the fallback independently because costs can shift at 5% rather than only above 10%. The redline is not minimal because it additionally requires audits to be “off-site where possible,” a restriction not needed to satisfy either stated position. Otherwise, the existing safeguards and commercial terms remain effective and no contradiction is introduced.
